name: Lancia Stratos Zero (Bertone)
hook: It has no doors at all: the entire windscreen hinges up and you climb in over the nose.
story: Turin, autumn 1970. Nuccio Bertone builds the Zero with nobody's money but his own, puts it on his stand at the motor show, and waits for Lancia to notice. Lancia does not. Not one executive walks across to look. So after the show he climbs in through the windscreen, drives to the Lancia works, and points the car at the closed barrier on the gate. He does not slow down. The car is 84 centimetres tall. It fits. "An astonished Lancia gatekeeper stared motionlessly at that strange object which was so low it could pass beneath his barrier," he remembered. The noise of the engine pulled the racing department out into the yard. Then the gatekeeper raised the bar. Cesare Fiorio ran that department, and he wanted a rally car built from nothing. What came out of it was the Stratos HF, which won the world rally championship in 1974, 1975 and 1976 with bodies built by Bertone.
description: The Stratos Zero is a one-off show car built by Carrozzeria Bertone in Turin and unveiled at the 1970 Turin Motor Show. Marcello Gandini drew it as a pure wedge, 846 mm tall, with no doors: the whole windscreen lifts and you step in over the nose. Behind the cockpit sits a 1.6-litre V4 taken from a Lancia Fulvia, under a triangular louvred cover. A band of 84 taillight bulbs runs across the tail.
